source_fields.instance: Arm $i$ has distribution $\nu_i=N(\mu_i,1)$, with $\mu\in\mathbb R^K$ and a unique best arm. For each fixed budget $T$, recommend after exactly $T$ fresh samples. Consider algorithm families $(A_T)$ whose error tends to zero on every admissible $\mu$, and compare asymptotic difficulty relative to the static allocation oracle that knows the instance.

view_override_policy.limitations: Mechanical merge does not certify consistency or mathematical identity. Narrative qualifications and source conditions remain authoritative.

source_fields.randomization: Private randomization is allowed. The seed is hidden from the environment and independent of the fixed instance and sample randomness.
source_fields.adaptivity: The action and every probe in a round may depend only on previous-round feedback, public inputs, any context or advice already revealed that round, and private randomness. They may not use unrevealed current losses or samples.
restrictions: The family $A=(A_T)_{T\ge1}$ is instancewise consistent: $p_{\mu,T}(A_T)\to0$ for every admissible $\mu$. Each $A_T$ may know $T$, but not $\mu$ or the static oracle allocation.
source_fields.internal_computation: Arbitrary measurable exact-real internal computation is allowed; feedback complexity implies no arithmetic or bit bound. The algorithm family must be instancewise consistent; polynomial time and known gaps are not assumed. Interpret T/log(1/p) as zero at p=0 and as positive infinity at p=1. Probabilities already integrate algorithmic and sample randomness, so no unspecified outer expectation is added.
source_fields.parallelism: Interaction proceeds in sequential time rounds. A two-point evaluation is one pair of same-round responses only where explicitly permitted; it is not equivalent to two independent rounds.

source_fields.complete_expression: The native target is $\inf_{\mathcal A\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{cons}}}\sup_{\mu:\ b(\mu)\ \mathrm{unique}}\limsup_{T\to\infty}\frac{T}{H_{\mathrm{so}}(\mu)\log(1/p_{\mu,T}(\mathcal A_T))}$.
aggregation_order: For each fixed μ, first integrate algorithmic and sampling randomness into the error probability p_{μ,T}.
Fix $\mu$ and take the asymptotic limsup of the relative difficulty as $T\to\infty$.
Then take the supremum over μ. The outermost infimum ranges over entire algorithm families that are consistent instance by instance.
Do not interchange $\sup_\mu$ and $\limsup_T$, or replace the asymptotic statement by a uniform finite-$T$ error-probability bound.
source_fields.quantifier_order: One algorithm must work for every μ. Static oracle may know μ only as a benchmark, not as learner input.
source_fields.time_uniformity: Each T specifies a separate fixed-budget algorithm A_T; the asymptotic comparison uses the complete uniform algorithm family.

description_paragraphs: The algorithm samples Gaussian arms under a fixed budget and recommends the best arm without knowing the instance's optimal static allocation. The comparison is between the asymptotic error exponent and the instance-informed static-allocation benchmark, with one algorithm sequence required to work on every instance.

interaction_timing: Fix mu; A_T receives public K, T, and variance one.

unresolved_applicability: The verified result is a lower bound on uniform relative asymptotic difficulty, not a uniformly optimal formula for every finite-budget error probability on one instance.
description_paragraphs: The Gaussian means $\mu$ are unknown. Variance is known and equals one; no common bounded interval is imposed on the means.
The algorithm family is $\mathcal{A}=(\mathcal{A}_T)_{T\ge1}$, with each $\mathcal{A}_T$ given the budget $T$. Consistency requires $p_{\mu,T}\to0$ for every admissible mean vector $\mu$.

The asymptotic static-oracle benchmark is $H_{\mathrm{so}}(\mu)$. Its optimal allocation may depend on the true means, which remain hidden from the learner. The natural exponential-family definition uses reverse divergence $\operatorname{KL}(\nu_{\lambda_i}\|\nu_{\mu_i})$; for unit-variance Gaussians it equals half the squared mean difference.
The model requires $K\ge2$, with algorithm budgets $T\ge1$. The registered nontrivial impossibility bound additionally requires $K\ge3$, which remains explicit in its region.

The set $\Delta_K^\circ$ is the probability simplex with strictly positive coordinates. In the alternative set $\operatorname{Alt}(\mu)$, the original best arm may tie with another arm or cease to be optimal.
